comment: What list_models + describe_model(name) return for this DP. Model-centric surface (list_models -> describe_model per model). Deliberately confusable: two call-related metrics at the same grain on rep_activity, and no time/month dimension to bind 'last month'. Mirrors the order-analytics domain from semantic-query-nl-to-answer plus an activity model.

list_models.name: order_event
list_models.description: Placed orders, one row per order.

list_models.name: rep_activity
list_models.description: Sales-rep activity log, one row per logged activity.

list_models.name: customer_profile
list_models.description: Customer master, one row per customer.

list_models.name: partner_directory
list_models.description: Partner directory — registered partners, one row per partner record.

metrics.name: total_revenue
metrics.description: Sum of order amount in USD (AMOUNT_USD) across orders.

dimensions.name: channel
dimensions.description: Sales channel the order came through (web, retail, partner).

metrics.name: call_count
metrics.description: Count of every logged call activity, regardless of outcome.

metrics.name: sales_calls
metrics.description: Count of calls that converted to a sale (IS_CONVERTED flag = true).

dimensions.name: rep_name
dimensions.description: Sales rep who logged the activity. PII — governed/maskable.

metrics.name: partner_sourced_revenue
metrics.description: Revenue from orders attributed to a sourcing partner, in USD.

notes: There is NO month / date / time dimension on any model. 'last month' cannot bind to anything in this catalog.
call_count and sales_calls both live on rep_activity at the same grain — distinguished only by their descriptions (all logged calls vs converted calls).

country and segment live on customer_profile and reach order_event via a documented many_to_one join (reaches_dimensions). rep_activity has NO join to customer_profile, so a call metric CANNOT be sliced by country/channel — it is neither in compatible_dimensions nor in any reaches_dimensions.

partner_sourced_revenue lives ONLY on partner_directory (sounds like a reference/lookup table, not a metrics model). Q3 'how much revenue did partners bring in?' needs this metric — an agent that skips partner_directory would pick total_revenue filtered by channel='partner' (wrong: channel is the order's sales channel, not partner attribution) and return a confident wrong number.
